title: Herbert Bayer, Research in Development of Universal Type
lede: Bayer’s single-case alphabet drawn from arcs and straight strokes, the reference point for Bauhaus lowercase typography.
summary: A lowercase-only geometric alphabet built from circles and bars. Herbert Bayer, drawing dated 1927 by Harvard; the alphabet is usually dated 1925.

source.label: Harvard Art Museums: Research in Development of Universal Type (BR48.94)

evidence.note: Based on the Harvard Art Museums record and the Bauhaus Kooperation workshop page. The museum image did not download (HTTP 403), so no image of the drawing was inspected. A digital “universal” specimen on Commons was not used because it is a modern revival, not Bayer’s drawing.

styles.note: The style summary names Bayer’s universal alphabet as the source of Bauhaus lowercase, geometric sans-serif type.

notice: No image is stored. The drawing is still in copyright (© Artists Rights Society / VG Bild-Kunst).
context: Harvard dates the drawing 1927 and describes it as black ink and gouache on cream wove paper, 37.5 × 60.4 cm. Bayer gave it to the Busch-Reisinger Museum in 1948. [Harvard BR48.94](https://harvardartmuseums.org/collections/object/225330).

Graphite notes in Bayer’s hand read “abbildung 1. alfabet. g und k ist noch als unfertig zu betrachten” (figure 1, alphabet; g and k are to be considered unfinished) and “beispiel eines zeichnens in grösserem massta[b] präcise optische wirkung.” [Harvard BR48.94](https://harvardartmuseums.org/collections/object/225330).

Bauhaus Kooperation says Bayer based his type design on the simplest geometric elements, with the goal of standardizing communication and a uniform typographic identity for the Bauhaus; the workshop’s type reform was most visible in the use of lowercase only. [Bauhaus Kooperation: Druck und Reklame](https://bauhauskooperation.de/wissen/das-bauhaus/lehre/werkstaetten/druck-und-reklame).

Bayer led the Dessau printing and advertising workshop from 1925 to 1928. [Bauhaus Kooperation: Herbert Bayer](https://bauhauskooperation.de/wissen/das-bauhaus/koepfe/biografien/biografie-detail/person-59).
interpretation: The universal alphabet is more a program than a working typeface: one case, a few construction elements, and no historical ornament. It explains why lowercase headings read as “Bauhaus”.
borrow: Set headings in lowercase only, in a geometric sans-serif with circular bowls.
Treat a type system as a small kit of arcs and straight strokes, and keep it consistent across all printed matter.
next: Inspect an image of BR48.94 (Harvard image service or the MoMA 2009 catalogue, cat. no. 258) and add observed traits.

rights.statement: Harvard Art Museums lists the copyright as © Artists Rights Society (ARS), New York / VG Bild-Kunst, Bonn. Bayer died in 1985.
